newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia nixes April PGM Japan shipment, May in doubt.
newsitem.headline: Russia nixes April PGM Japan shipment, May in doubt.

text.p: A Russian official in Tokyo said on Monday there would be no Russian shipments of platinum group metals to Japan in April and that May shipments were also in doubt.

"Almaz (Russia's platinum group metal export agency) can say for sure that there will be no Russian PGM (platinum group metal) shipments to Japan in April and there is still uncertainty if the May delivery to Japan will take place," Y.F. Zhigulov, the trade representative of the Russian Federation in Japan, told Reuters.
He was reading a note from the Almaz head office in Moscow.
"We don't know yet when the Japan-Russia export contract talks for PGMs will take place as Almaz has not yet received the export licence for PGMs," he said.
He also said Russian PGM exports for 1997 would be much lower than in 1996.
The latest round of annual Japan-Russia talks on PGM export contracts, usually held in mid-December, were postponed indefinitely due to Russian domestic considerations.
Talks were initially held up by the delayed passage of the Russia's 1997 federal budget and by recent cabinet changes, and are now awaiting a government decree.
Russia is the world's largest producer of palladium, a key platinum group metal, and Japan is the biggest consumer.
